mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about an infinite set is correct?

options.A: It is a set that contains an unbounded number of elements, such as the set of natural numbers.
options.B: It is a set that contains every possible element of the universe.
options.C: It has the same number of elements as the empty set.

mcqs.answer: It is a set that contains an unbounded number of elements, such as the set of natural numbers.
mcqs.explanation: An infinite set is one that is not finite; its elements cannot be listed completely because there is no last element. Option A correctly describes this. Option B is impossible, Option C confuses cardinality with emptiness, and Option D describes a singleton, not an infinite set.

mcqs.question: If a set S contains exactly one element, which of the following correctly defines S?

options.D: S is a finite set with more than one element.

mcqs.explanation: A set with precisely one element is called a singleton set. Hence option A is correct. Option B describes a set with no elements, option C describes a set with unlimited elements, and option D contradicts the premise of having exactly one element.

mcqs.question: Consider the two sets A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {4, 3, 2, 1}. Which statement is true?

options.A: A and B are equal sets because they contain exactly the same elements.
options.B: A and B are not equal because the order of elements is different.
options.C: A and B are not equal because the elements are listed differently.
options.D: A and B are equal only because they have the same number of elements.

mcqs.answer: A and B are equal sets because they contain exactly the same elements.
mcqs.explanation: Two sets are equal if they have precisely the same elements, irrespective of order or repetition. Hence A is correct. Options B and C incorrectly treat order as relevant, and D confuses equality with equivalence (same cardinality).

mcqs.question: Which pair of sets are equivalent (i.e., have the same number of elements)?
mcqs.explanation: Equivalent sets have the same cardinality. Both sets in option A contain three elements, so they are equivalent. Option B has 2 vs 1 element, C has 0 vs 1, and D has 4 vs 3 elements, none of which are equivalent.

mcqs.question: What is the correct definition of the empty set?

options.A: A set that contains no elements, denoted by ∅.
options.B: A set that contains exactly one element.
options.C: A set that contains infinitely many elements.
options.D: A set that contains only the number zero.

mcqs.answer: A set that contains no elements, denoted by ∅.
mcqs.explanation: The empty set, also called the null set, has no elements at all and is represented by ∅ or {}. Options B, C, and D describe other types of sets.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a finite set?

options.A: A set that contains a countable number of elements which can be listed completely.
options.B: A set that contains an infinite number of elements.
options.C: A set that contains no elements.
options.D: A set that contains exactly one element.

mcqs.answer: A set that contains a countable number of elements which can be listed completely.
mcqs.explanation: A finite set has a limited number of elements; therefore it can be enumerated entirely. Options B describes an infinite set, C describes the empty set (which is also finite but the definition focuses on limited non‑zero count), and D is a special case of a finite set but does not capture the general definition.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines an infinite set and distinguishes it from a finite set?

options.A: An infinite set has an unbounded number of elements, such as the set of natural numbers, whereas a finite set has a limited number of elements.
options.B: An infinite set contains exactly one element, while a finite set contains none.
options.C: An infinite set is the same as the empty set, while a finite set contains infinitely many elements.
options.D: An infinite set has a fixed number of elements, just like a finite set.

mcqs.answer: An infinite set has an unbounded number of elements, such as the set of natural numbers, whereas a finite set has a limited number of elements.
mcqs.explanation: Option A accurately captures the definition of an infinite set and contrasts it with a finite set. The other options invert or confuse the concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets is a singleton set?
mcqs.explanation: A singleton set contains exactly one element; {7} meets this criterion. Option B is the empty set, C has two elements, and D has five elements.
